entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emmanuel-Félicité de Durfort, duc de Duras, born into one of France's most ancient and powerful noble families on December 19, 1715, in Paris, embodied the apex of Ancien Régime aristocracy, serving as a Marshal of France, diplomat, and peer. His career spanned the reigns of Louis XV and Louis XVI, positioning him at the heart of French military and political affairs during a period of intense geopolitical flux in Western Europe. As a grandee of the realm and a prominent Freemason, Duras navigated the complex social and political currents that ultimately led to the French Revolution, representing a class whose influence was both deeply entrenched and increasingly challenged.

His extensive career saw him rise through military ranks, notably participating in the War of the Austrian Succession and distinguishing himself during the Seven Years' War (1756-1763) where he commanded forces in Germany. From 1755 to 1758, Duras served as the French Ambassador to Spain, a crucial diplomatic post that underscored the Franco-Spanish Bourbon alliance. Elevated to Marshal of France in 1775, he also held the governorship of Franche-Comté and was a key figure in the Parlement de Paris, where he defended aristocratic prerogatives. Beyond state service, he became the Grand Master of the Grand Orient de France in 1772, a testament to his influence within burgeoning Enlightenment-era social networks.
